newsitem.title: UK: Gold shares may fall after high volatility-analyst.
newsitem.headline: Gold shares may fall after high volatility-analyst.

text.p: Volatility in gold shares is at a record high compared with movement in the spot gold price, which may point to a large price move in one of the two markets, a leading metals analyst said.
A sharp rise in the ratio usually presages a big move higher by bullion, but this time shares may be in for a fall, Andy Smith of Union Bank of Switzerland said in a commentary.
The volatility of the Philadelphia XAU index of major gold mining shares is around 33 percent while volatility for spot gold is under 3.0 percent, he said.
Since June the XAU index has dived from around 150 to a low of 114, settling at 128.19 on Monday.
During the same period spot gold has been stuck in a narrow range between $380 and $390.
"Records show that such "hot spots' have been good lead indicators of major launches in the gold price," Smith said.
That happened in 1989, 1993 and 1995, but on this occasion the pattern may be different, he added.

"Turning the telescope around, it may be that gold shares simply built in too much hope about volatility in the underlying metal and are due for a big correction (down) whatever the gold price does," Smith said.
"In this case, a gold miner should be issuing paper or options on his paper faster than you could say 'overvaluation', then using the premium income to buy gold puts," he added.
